name: PostHog
summary: A product suite presented as a place to explore, rather than a stack of interchangeable cards.

observations.hero: A desktop-like shell surrounds a central window. Navigation icons sit on both sides; the introduction and signup panel share a row.
observations.typography: Bold compact sans-serif headings; body text stays conversational. Colored inline highlights reinforce key terms.
observations.visual_system: Green illustrated environment, translucent pale window, orange beveled actions and vividly colored story tabs.
observations.page_sequence: Introduction → illustrative product tabs → tool inventory → customers → data warehouse → pricing → company rationale → reading → deliberately playful closing CTA.
observations.interaction: Clicked Ship with PostHog. The selected tab and product story changed, with sample inbox reports replacing the earlier assistant story. A pause control was present but not tested.
observations.accessibility: Semantic structure inspected through browser accessibility output. No contrast, keyboard, screen-reader or reduced-motion audit was completed.

principles: Give a broad suite a navigable mental model.
Let expressive brand elements organize information instead of merely decorating it.
Identify illustrative data as illustrative.
interpretation.fit: Choose this approach only if it explains the audience’s actual evaluation task.
interpretation.risks: Desktop chrome competes for attention; nested scrolling needs separate mobile and keyboard testing.

limitations: Single browser, single inspection date; homepage content can change.
Exact font names, animation timing and implementation libraries were not verified.
Tablet, mobile and reduced-motion behavior remain unverified.
Only selected regions were visually inspected; section sequence also uses rendered DOM. This is not a complete deep audit.

name: Resend
summary: Editorial type and generous silence open a long, increasingly concrete product tour for developer email infrastructure.

observations.hero: At 1363 × 936, a left-aligned two-line serif headline moves from bright white to gray on black; Get started and Documentation sit beneath the brief explanation. A faint light ray gives the largely open right side a focal point. A slim navigation bar stays at the top while scrolling.
observations.typography: High-contrast display serif paired with plain sans-serif body and monospace code. Exact families unverified.
observations.visual_system: Black surfaces, white display text, subtle lighting and finely outlined code panels. The integration chapter uses a large envelope symbol and a centered gradient-accented heading before the language chooser. Wide negative space alternates with dense product windows, making the change in information density intentional.
observations.page_sequence: Full-page desktop scan: open hero → customer logos → integration code window → paired Test mode and Modular webhooks → Editor demo → contacts and analytics pair → React Email code and preview → deliverability grid → single testimonial → dashboard controls → testimonial carousel → large serif closing statement and footer. The page is roughly 12,352 px tall in this captured viewport; the exact length depends on browser rendering.
observations.interaction: Clicked Python in the integration code chooser. The main language and nested example tabs both selected Python, and the visible snippet changed to Python. The dashboard tabs and testimonial carousel were seen in the full-page capture but were not operated. No email was sent.
observations.accessibility: Semantic structure inspected through browser accessibility output. No contrast, keyboard, screen-reader or reduced-motion audit was completed.

principles: Make technical adoption concrete with a short, relevant integration example.
A quiet hero can precede dense functional explanation.
Use typographic contrast to create identity without obscuring product meaning.
interpretation.fit: Choose this approach only if it explains the audience’s actual evaluation task.
interpretation.risks: Some body text appears subdued against black. The long sequence and dense product windows demand careful small-screen pacing. A full-page capture does not establish the behavior of unclicked tabs or carousels.

limitations: Single browser, single inspection date; homepage content can change.
Exact font names, animation timing and implementation libraries were not verified.
Tablet, mobile and reduced-motion behavior remain unverified.

Hero, middle and footer regions plus a full-page desktop capture were visually inspected; the Python control was operated. Other interactive controls, keyboard and assistive-technology behavior were not tested.

name: Onlook
summary: A visual engineering tool explains itself through the language of a working canvas.

observations.hero: Centered lightweight sans-serif statement; paired design/demo actions lead into a large editor canvas.
observations.typography: Large lightweight sans-serif display and muted body text. The long FAQ uses a spacious split heading-and-question layout.
observations.visual_system: Near-black and dark gray surfaces, thin rules, broad editor imagery and restrained white actions.
observations.page_sequence: Hero → canvas → code-aware design features → workflow capabilities → stack compatibility → community → FAQ → final action/footer.
observations.interaction: Clicked the free-version FAQ question. aria-expanded changed to true. The hero showed “Error loading scene” in this browser; the intended scene was not evaluated.
observations.accessibility: Semantic structure inspected through browser accessibility output. No contrast, keyboard, screen-reader or reduced-motion audit was completed.

principles: Present the workspace as the product’s explanatory medium.
Demonstrate continuity between visual editing and real code.
Keep essential messaging and actions usable when a rich scene fails.
interpretation.fit: Choose this approach only if it explains the audience’s actual evaluation task.
interpretation.risks: The observed hero scene failure makes this an instructive resilience case, not an unqualified quality endorsement.

limitations: Single browser, single inspection date; homepage content can change.
Exact font names, animation timing and implementation libraries were not verified.
Tablet, mobile and reduced-motion behavior remain unverified.
Only selected regions were visually inspected; section sequence also uses rendered DOM. This is not a complete deep audit.

name: Mercury
summary: A cinematic opening connects business finance to the world the founder wants to build.

observations.hero: Centered statement and signup/demo actions sit over a landscape with a desk in the foreground. A financial-service disclaimer is visible at the bottom.
observations.typography: Clean sans-serif rather than an assumed editorial serif. Medium-weight heading contrasts with lighter supporting copy.
observations.visual_system: Landscape imagery, muted sky tones, dark navy product regions and electric blue primary actions.
observations.page_sequence: Immersive hero → product categories → customer proof → onboarding and capability explanations → company narrative/news → business/personal actions → legal footnotes.
observations.interaction: Opened Products. A large multicolumn menu exposed banking, cards, payments and intelligence categories. No account application or demo transaction was submitted.
observations.accessibility: Semantic structure inspected through browser accessibility output. No contrast, keyboard, screen-reader or reduced-motion audit was completed.

principles: Pair an aspirational opening with concrete product explanation.
Keep material product qualifications close to the promise.
Give a broad offer a navigable category structure.
interpretation.fit: Choose this approach only if it explains the audience’s actual evaluation task.
interpretation.risks: Foreground text competes with the landscape. Navigation overlay obscured some lower-page review; full-page and responsive inspection still needed.

limitations: Single browser, single inspection date; homepage content can change.
Exact font names, animation timing and implementation libraries were not verified.
Tablet, mobile and reduced-motion behavior remain unverified.
Only selected regions were visually inspected; section sequence also uses rendered DOM. This is not a complete deep audit.

name: Linear
summary: Product context occupies the space that generic homepages fill with decoration.

observations.hero: Large left-aligned sans-serif statement followed by a broad issue-management interface with an agent conversation layered alongside it.
observations.typography: Large regular sans-serif heading, subdued supporting copy and compact interface labels.
observations.visual_system: Near-black canvas, subtle gray dividers, broad UI panels and limited accent color.
observations.page_sequence: Hero/product interface → rationale → intake → planning → AI/automations → building/review → changelog → closing CTA/footer.
observations.interaction: Opened Product menu and observed grouped workflow destinations. Escape returned visible keyboard focus to the trigger. App-like hero controls were not functionally verified.
observations.accessibility: Semantic structure inspected through browser accessibility output. No contrast, keyboard, screen-reader or reduced-motion audit was completed.

principles: Use a recognizable work artifact to make the product concrete.
Organize page architecture around the lifecycle of work.
Limit visual accents so product state carries emphasis.
interpretation.fit: Choose this approach only if it explains the audience’s actual evaluation task.
interpretation.risks: A rich hero can imply more interactivity than exists. Do not copy controls unless they have useful behavior.

limitations: Single browser, single inspection date; homepage content can change.
Exact font names, animation timing and implementation libraries were not verified.
Tablet, mobile and reduced-motion behavior remain unverified.

name: Firecrawl
summary: A technical API turns its main operation into the homepage entrance.

observations.hero: Centered headline, orange emphasis and an operation field with Search/Scrape/Map/Crawl controls; output preview follows immediately.
observations.typography: Confident sans-serif display with monospace metadata and code; ordinary body copy explains the operation.
observations.visual_system: Pale ruled grid, orange actions, small technical markers, code/output surfaces and a saturated orange narrative interruption.
observations.page_sequence: Hero/operation preview → customer strip → API/code samples → agent setup → performance claims → capability grid → use cases → library narrative → community → CTA → FAQ/footer.
observations.interaction: Clicked Scrape. The action destination changed to a scrape-mode playground URL and the preview displayed structured output. No remote scrape was submitted.
observations.accessibility: Semantic structure inspected through browser accessibility output. No contrast, keyboard, screen-reader or reduced-motion audit was completed.

principles: Show the shape of input and output before listing features.
Let technical affordances become a visual motif.
Interrupt long neutral sections with one purposeful color field.
interpretation.fit: Choose this approach only if it explains the audience’s actual evaluation task.
interpretation.risks: Benchmark claims belong to the company and were not independently validated. Pale microtext and extensive scrolling deserve accessibility checks.

limitations: Single browser, single inspection date; homepage content can change.
Exact font names, animation timing and implementation libraries were not verified.
Tablet, mobile and reduced-motion behavior remain unverified.
Full-page composition and selected interaction states inspected on desktop; this does not imply responsive verification.

name: Raycast

observations.hero: Centered short headline and download action against black, followed by a launcher demonstration.
observations.typography: Bold compact sans-serif headings, short body copy and monospace installation metadata.
observations.visual_system: Dark canvas, floating product surfaces, red and blue accents, framed extension panels and generous vertical gaps.
observations.page_sequence: Hero → launcher preview → rationale → extension gallery → AI tools → professional proof → automation → notes → community → developer tools → final download/footer.
observations.interaction: Full-page composition inspected. A workflow button seen during initial load could not be located after hydration, so its behavior is not verified. Download actions were not activated.
observations.accessibility: Semantic structure inspected through browser accessibility output. No contrast, keyboard, screen-reader or reduced-motion audit was completed.

principles: Use one interaction grammar across many capabilities.
Alternate overview and close-up product views.
Make platform requirements visible near the action.
interpretation.fit: Choose this approach only if it explains the audience’s actual evaluation task.
interpretation.risks: Initial-load and hydrated controls differed in this browser. Large blank intervals in a full-page capture may include unrevealed scroll content; do not infer animation implementation.

limitations: Single browser, single inspection date; homepage content can change.
Exact font names, animation timing and implementation libraries were not verified.
Tablet, mobile and reduced-motion behavior remain unverified.
Full-page composition and selected interaction states inspected on desktop; this does not imply responsive verification.

name: Stripe
summary: Enterprise breadth is organized through business models and implementation paths.

observations.hero: A broad left-aligned typographic statement overlays a colorful diagonal field; signup actions and a logo strip form a clear lower boundary.
observations.typography: Large regular sans-serif statement with differences in text tone inside the same paragraph.
observations.visual_system: White base, precise thin rules, purple actions and a large multicolor diagonal visual.
observations.page_sequence: Hero → business-model solutions → global scale → customer segments/cases → developer infrastructure → news → CTA/footer.
observations.interaction: Opened Products. The expanded navigation grouped payment capabilities and revealed individual product destinations. Solution demonstrations were not tested.
observations.accessibility: Semantic structure inspected through browser accessibility output. No contrast, keyboard, screen-reader or reduced-motion audit was completed.

principles: Structure a broad platform by customer decisions.
Use a large visual field to create direction without enclosing every sentence in a card.
Separate business narrative from developer integration detail.
interpretation.fit: Choose this approach only if it explains the audience’s actual evaluation task.
interpretation.risks: This mature platform’s breadth is inappropriate for a narrow early-stage product. Homepage claims were observed, not independently verified.

limitations: Single browser, single inspection date; homepage content can change.
Exact font names, animation timing and implementation libraries were not verified.
Tablet, mobile and reduced-motion behavior remain unverified.
Full-page composition and the expanded navigation were inspected on desktop. Some scroll-triggered visuals remained blank in the full-page capture; their behavior is unverified.
